scope: One user-authorized same-input short-shot lighting comparison on the retained RTX 3090, plus decoding the exact same sampled latent with old settings

ceilingExposure.method: Motion-compensated adjacent-frame median log2 linear-luminance ratio in a selected stable ceiling patch; descriptors are not whole-image or perceptual quality scores

framing.measurementLimit: Face boxes measure apparent head scale/center, not physical camera depth, whole-body pose, or identity similarity

observed: Visible later exposure pulse removed with continuous decoding and recreated by same-latent tiled control
Less pronounced mid-shot smoothing in the combined candidate; individual sampler/relight contributions not isolated
Reference hair/outfit and broad appearance remain recognizable
Source deliberately holds an open-mouth expression and sideward gaze
remainingIssues: Candidate sometimes reduces mouth opening and increases brow furrowing relative to source
Center positioning is less precise than earlier Fast control, though sampled checks pass
Background is regenerated; no pixel-exact preservation or general identity guarantee

decision.historicalContinuations: Previous decoder preserved for jobs without renderVersion
decision.naturalPreset: optional experimental; not promoted based on mixed acting/framing result

memory.limitation: Sampled across primary render and decoder diagnostic; not a guaranteed peak or an isolated decoder memory benchmark

connectionRecovery.fix: Safe GETs: 45-second deadline, at most three attempts, abortable 500/1000ms backoff; POSTs never replayed automatically

limitations: One short single-person shot, no long-shot/30fps quality proof
Lighting control isolates decoder effect; combined primary changes do not isolate relight vs sampler effect
No automated identity or expression-fidelity score
Native VAE may fall back to tiled decoding for other memory conditions
artifacts: Raw user media, graphs, history, latent, dense comparison sheets and telemetry retained only in ignored local storage
